best-octopus-go-alternative.html.pre: * All rates pulled 26 September 2026. Octopus Go: GO-FIX-12M-26-09-18. EDF: EDF_EV_FIX_GOELEC_12M_V3_HH (Go Electric 12m v3) and EDF_EV_FIX_GOELEC_18M_V3_HH (Go Electric 18m v3). EDF has changed its mind twice in a week. The 12m v3 launched on 18 September with higher peak rates and standing charges, was closed on 23 September with the older, cheaper v2 offered in its place, and was reopened at 18:00 on 25 September when v2 was withdrawn again. The 12-month figures here are v3, which is what EDF's quote journey offers today; the 18-month v3, introduced on 23 September, is unchanged. The two EDF tariffs no longer share a standing charge. The 18-month is about 3.5p/kWh cheaper at peak and nearly 6p a day cheaper on standing charge than the 12-month, so on today's prices it is the cheaper EDF tariff on every line except the exit fee (£100 rather than £75) and the six-month longer tie-in. Both keep the 6.99p/kWh off-peak rate. Against Octopus Go, the 18-month has the lower peak rate in every region and is within a penny or so a day on standing charge. The 12-month has the lower peak rate everywhere except London, but its standing charge is 5.5 to 6.5p a day higher than Octopus Go’s in every region. On 18 September 2026 Octopus raised prices too, but in a particular way: they set the new pre-VAT off-peak rate to exactly the old including-VAT rate, in all 14 regions. So from 1 October, when VAT on electricity drops to 0%, you pay the same overnight rate as before the rise — Octopus keeps the VAT cut rather than passing it on. Until 30 September you pay 5% more than you did. Their peak rate is a genuine increase either way, and their standing charge is slightly lower after the cut. All figures include VAT at 5%. Note that VAT on domestic electricity in Great Britain drops from 5% to 0% between 1 October 2026 and 31 March 2027, which will cut every rate here by about 4.8% — suppliers' own quotes may already be shown at 0%. Rates are baked into this page at time of writing — always verify on each supplier's website before switching.
